lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: formal constructions with compass, straightedge, and dynamic tools
lessonRef.title: Assessment preparation: formal constructions with compass, straightedge, and dynamic tools

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Which statement is a precise definition of a circle?
choices: a shape whose area is πr²
a polygon with infinitely many sides
a closed curve with no corners
the set of all points in a plane at a fixed distance from a given centre point

items.prompt: A construction proceeds as follows. Through point P not on line ℓ, copy the angle that a transversal makes with ℓ, placing the copy at P on the same transversal. What has been constructed?
choices: a line through P parallel to ℓ
a line through P perpendicular to ℓ
the reflection of ℓ across P
the perpendicular bisector of the transversal

items.prompt: A regular hexagon is inscribed in a circle of radius 7. What central angle does each side subtend?
Which statement correctly justifies the perpendicular bisector construction?
choices: The compass width was more than half the segment, which forces perpendicularity.
Any line through the midpoint is a perpendicular bisector.
Both constructed points are equidistant from the endpoints, and the locus of such points is exactly the perpendicular bisector.
The arcs look symmetric, so the line must be perpendicular.

items.prompt: Which statement is a precise definition of a perpendicular lines?
choices: two lines that never meet
two lines that form an isosceles triangle
two lines that intersect to form right angles
two lines with opposite slopes

items.prompt: A construction proceeds as follows. With the compass set to the radius, mark successive arcs around the circle from a starting point, then join consecutive marks. What has been constructed?
choices: a regular hexagon inscribed in the circle
a square inscribed in the circle
an equilateral triangle inscribed in the circle
a regular pentagon inscribed in the circle

items.prompt: A regular hexagon is inscribed in a circle of radius 8. What central angle does each side subtend?
Which statement correctly justifies the equilateral triangle construction on a given segment?
choices: Both circles have radius equal to the segment, so all three sides are that same length.
The construction works only when the segment is horizontal.
The intersection point is the midpoint of the segment.
The circles intersect, which guarantees 60° angles by definition.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: Which statement is a precise definition of a line segment?
choices: the shortest path between two shapes
part of a line that goes on forever in one direction
the set of two endpoints and all points between them on the line through them
a line with a measurable length

items.prompt: A construction proceeds as follows. Open the compass to more than half of AB. From A draw an arc above and below AB; from B, with the same opening, draw arcs crossing them. Draw the line through the two crossing points. What has been constructed?
choices: the angle bisector of ∠A
a line parallel to AB
a copy of segment AB
the perpendicular bisector of AB

items.prompt: A regular triangle is inscribed in a circle of radius 5. What central angle does each side subtend?
Which statement correctly justifies the angle bisector construction?
choices: Equal arcs always produce equal angles regardless of the triangle.
The construction builds two congruent triangles by SSS, so the angles at the vertex are congruent.
The ray drawn appears to split the angle evenly.
The construction relies on the angle being acute.
